title: When the API Speaks the Wrong Language: Revisiting Post-Training for Multilingual Tool Use
abstract: arXiv:2608.11715v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The reliability of Large Language Models (LLMs) for API calling degrades in multilingual settings. A common failure occurs when a model selects the correct tool but generates argument values in an inconsistent language, which we term Argument Language Mismatch (ALM). Although semantically correct, such outputs are operationally invalid and not captured by standard API-calling metrics. We revisit post-training strategies for mitigating ALM and find that, in our benchmark, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) provides a strong baseline, substantially improving argument language consistency and end-to-end function call accuracy. Under consistent model selection, SFT achieves performance comparable to, and sometimes exceeding more complex reinforcement learning (RL) approaches. translated_title: 当API说错语言：重新审视多语言工具使用的后训练方法
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）在API调用中的可靠性在多语言环境下会下降。一个常见的失败模式是模型选择了正确的工具，但生成的参数值使用了不一致的语言，我们称之为参数语言不匹配（ALM）。尽管这些输出在语义上是正确的，但在操作上无效，并且未被标准的API调用指标捕获。我们重新审视了缓解ALM的后训练策略，并在我们的基准测试中发现，监督微调（SFT）提供了一个强大的基线，显著提高了参数语言一致性和端到端函数调用准确性。在一致的模型选择下，SFT的性能可与更复杂的强化学习（RL）方法相媲美，有时甚至超过它们。我们进一步研究了具有结构化、参数感知奖励的RL是否能带来额外的好处。虽然像组相对策略优化（GRPO）这样的方法可以改善某些方面，但未完全解决ALM问题。
tldr: 本论文发现监督微调（SFT）在多语言API调用中能有效解决参数语言不匹配问题，其性能可与甚至超越更复杂的强化学习方法。
en_tdlr: This paper finds that supervised fine-tuning (SFT) effectively mitigates Argument Language Mismatch in multilingual API calling, achieving performance comparable to or exceeding more complex reinforcement learning methods.
